newsitem.title: GERMANY: German banks brace for Deutsche Telekom listing.
newsitem.headline: German banks brace for Deutsche Telekom listing.

text.p: As German banks stopped taking orders for stock in Deutsche Telekom on Thursday, the financial community geared up for record turnover next week when Europe's biggest-ever stock offering will be launched.

Expecting record volumes from first-time trading in Telekom shares, bank employees are putting in overtime hours and German stock exchanges are bracing for extended trading hours next week to handle the additional business.
The German DAX of 30 leading stocks is expected to continue rallying Friday ahead of Deutsche Telekom's flotation.
"We hope our systems can deal with the volumes," said a Frankfurt banker, who asked not to be identified.

Banks around the country reported robust business ahead of the 2 p.m. deadline to place orders for shares of the German telecommunications giant, which will begin trading on stock markets around the world for the first time Monday.

The day marked one of the busiest periods after the rush of buy orders Nov. 6, the last day when people registered with Telekom's share information centre (AIF) were able to buy discounted shares and take advantage of other benefits.

Around 3 billion shares in Deutsche Telekom have been ordered by individual and institutional investors, which amounts to approximately a fivefold oversubscription of the landmark offering, Telekom and banking sources said.

Facing overwhelming demand, Telekom topped up the issue by 20 percent earlier this week. It will now float up to 690 million shares, or around 25 percent of its capital. Another 30 million shares will be sold to Telekom employees.
The final share price will be set Sunday.
